claim: The ILO publicly disowned the only recent Philippine platform-worker earnings figures in circulation, stating they came from an unvalidated draft and that assertions workers earn 'well above minimum wage' are not official ILO conclusions.
stance_target: The claim that authoritative quantitative income evidence for Southeast Asian platform and creator work does not currently exist, and that circulating figures are unvalidated
scope_conditions: Philippines, statement dated 26 February 2026; covers transport network vehicle service drivers and delivery riders, adjacent to but not identical with content creators
quoted_support: The material cited in recent media coverage is drawn from a draft document currently undergoing technical validation. It is not a published report, not final, not endorsed, and does not represent an official ILO position.

claim: The ILO specifies that a credible platform-work earnings figure must distinguish gross from net income and account for operating costs, unpaid waiting time, working-time intensity, overtime hours and income volatility -- criteria that essentially no published creator income statistic meets.
stance_target: The validity of reported creator income figures that quote gross brand-deal, affiliate or ad revenue without netting production costs, unpaid pitching and production time, or month-to-month volatility
scope_conditions: Philippines, February 2026; stated by the ILO country office as a general methodological requirement for platform-work earnings assessment
quoted_support: Proper assessment of earnings requires distinguishing between gross and net income and accounting for operating costs, unpaid waiting time, working-time intensity, overtime hours, and income volatility.

claim: Philippine labour groups publicly disputed the leaked platform-worker earnings findings, showing that even the direction of the finding is contested within the country it describes.
stance_target: The claim that Southeast Asian platform-income figures should not be reported without noting that they are contested and unvalidated
scope_conditions: Philippines, February 2026; evidenced by the ILO's own linked press coverage (BusinessWorld 17 Feb 2026, BusinessMirror 18 Feb 2026, Malaya)
quoted_support: The integrity of evidence matters. Preliminary technical work must not be used in ways that distort public discourse or undermine the objective of advancing decent work and social justice.
numbers: 3 press items linked by the ILO
